chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: WPA music in the 1930s
summary: Musicians on WPA earned about twenty-five dollars a week to rehearse and play in parks; Spikes was refused because he owned property.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: What was happening in music during the '30s here? Very much? I know that was Depression years but...

Well, all the musicians on WPA. They paid 'em, I think, uh, I don't know, twenty...twenty-five dollars a week to re... you rehearsed all...every morning two hours, and then on Saturday you played in a park or somewhere a couple of hours. But that was...that was a...generally, that kept you livin', you know--twenty-five dollars or so a week but they wouldn't let me on there.

Because I had property worth more than five thousand dollars. If you had o...if you had some, uh, that was worth five thousand dollars, you couldn't get on that program. So all of the musicians was on there, and on Saturdays or Sundays, they'd play in a park or somewhere for coupla hours. But you see, they had all their nights. They catch three or four nights a week with the extra little money that
the government was payin' 'em, why it kinda carried 'em over.
